messages.subject: seeds, variograms and bounded ESS?
parts:
1. I coded up the Seeds example from vol 1 of
BUGS and committed it with a makefile to run it.
All in:

$STAN/src/models/bugs_examples/vol1/seeds

It's a simple logistic regression with an
intercept, two predictors, and the interaction of
the two predictors.

After dumping the results into R and calculating
means and variances, it gets the same answers as BUGS!

It takes about 3s to run 2000 samples (the first
1000 of which are then discarded). It should be a bit
faster when we tune the gamma calcs as we've done for
the normal.


2. Is there an implementation of the variogram
ESS stuff in R that I could use?

If not, Matt says he can code one.


3. I'm transforming the samples back from their
unbounded representations to the constrained ones
as part of output (e.g., using scale rather than
log scale parameters). But I realize given that these
are non-linear transforms that they can effect ESS.

We'll measure ESS on the constrained parameters,
not the unconstrained ones, right?


- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] (un)transformed Rhat/ESS?
parts:
On 11/25/11 4:31 PM, Andrew Gelman wrote:
> In the original R-hat paper, we recommend monitoring on parameters
> transformed to continuous scales, just because that seems to make
> sense, given that we're working with means and variances.

We're only talking about continuous parameters for now.

I'm pretty sure that R2WinBUGS and R2jags calculate
R-hat using the positive-only deviation (or variance or
precision) parameters, rather than applying a log transform.
R2jags even treats a 5-way categorical variable as a
continuous variable in [1,5] instead of using a 4-way (or
5-way) binary encoding. (The other problem with monitoring
discrete parameters for mixtures is that often 1000 samples
all put a point in the same mixture component and therefore
get an effective sample size of 1.)

This is going to be a huge amount of work if we have to
transform all the JAGS models' outputs. Although we have the
transform code, we don't have the variable typings we
need to synch the transforms with JAGS's output. I'm not
even sure how we could do that in general without writing
another language for specifying it and parsing it or just
writing one-off code for each model, either of which is likely
to be error prone (as is our recoding, but we test our output
vs. that reported in BUGS).

The transforms are trivial for deviation and binomial
parameters, but much less so for ordered logit cutpoints,
multinomial parameters and covariance matrices.

- Bob

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] (un)transformed Rhat/ESS?
parts: When I wrote the original R-hat function, it had an option to specify varaibles to be transformed as log or logit, and that's what I've done in my applications.  But it's not a really big deal.  If we want to be consistent with Jags we can monitor on the original scale.  We also have nonparametric versions of R-hat and ESS but, as you keep reminding us, these are more difficult to compute!

parts:
> When I wrote the original R-hat function, it had an option to specify
> varaibles to be transformed as log or logit, and that's what I've
> done in my applications. But it's not a really big deal. If we want
> to be consistent with Jags we can monitor on the original scale.

Great -- that will make life much easier.

It's the same two-point outline you put on the board:

1. We can do the right thing in Stan -- we have
all the transformed variables at hand to monitor.

We'll be able to do that and return samples on the
original untransformed scale.

It might be a little hard for users to understand R-hat for
the transformed multivariate params, but at least they'll
see which covariance parameter or set of cutpoints
is not converging.

2. For comparison with JAGS, we'll measure R-hat and
ESS for Stan and JAGS using the untransformed variables
following the practice in R2jags/Coda.

> also have nonparametric versions of R-hat and ESS but, as you keep
> reminding us, these are more difficult to compute!

That was probably Matt or Kenny. Are those defs also in
the original paper?

- Bob

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] (un)transformed Rhat/ESS?
parts:
There are some ideas in my 1998 paper with Steve Brooks.  But the simplest version is to first pre-process the sims by rank-transforming them, then apply R-hat and ESS from there.  The difficulty is that when you get new sims, you need to reapply the rank transformation all over again.
A
